content.title: About
content.content: Pickled celery consists of celery stalks that have been brined with vinegar, spices, and sometimes sugar. It has a crisp texture and a mildly sour, aromatic flavor that makes it a popular ingredient in salads, appetizers, and Asian dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Celery belongs to the Apiaceae family and is closely related to parsley and dill.
Pickling retains most of the B‑vitamins and minerals such as potassium and folate.
In Russia, pickled celery is often served as a snack with vodka.
Celery contains phthalides, compounds that may help lower blood pressure.
Celery stalks can be used as a natural flavoring in cocktails.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Celery provides flavonoids and vitamin C, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Nitrate compounds in celery may promote vessel dilation and reduce blood pressure.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium assists in fluid balance and muscle function.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C and other phytonutrients help strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to celery, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Pickled celery often contains a lot of salt, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: Large amounts may cause gas and discomfort in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Vinegar content
items.content: Vinegar can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pickled celery is used in salads, sandwiches, sushi rolls, as a garnish for meat or fish, and even in cocktails. Slice it into thin rounds or strips and serve as a snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated in its original brine in a sealed jar. When stored properly, it stays fresh for 3–4 weeks. Discard if mold appears or an off‑odor develops.
